items.statement:
Use the smooth finite Grassmann-valued chiral fields, conjugate-linear anti-automorphism, left derivatives and ordered coefficient-extraction integrals of Four-dimensional N=1 superspace Grassmann algebra and Berezin integration and Four-dimensional N=1 chiral superfield on flat superspace. Write $I_D(U)$ for the coefficient of $\theta^1\theta^2\bar\theta^{\dot1}\bar\theta^{\dot2}$ and $I_F(Y)$ for the coefficient of $\theta^1\theta^2$ in a chiral field. These raw mathematical integrals are unchanged. Define the physical action brackets by

$$[U]_D:=-\frac14 I_D(U),\qquad [Y]_F:=\frac12 I_F(Y).$$

A Hermitian conjugate in a physical F action means the conjugate of the extracted coefficient, added once. It does not mean replacing that operation by an unadjusted raw ordered antichiral integral. Physical chiral component names are fixed by

$$\Phi(y,\theta)=\phi(y)+\sqrt2\theta^\alpha\psi_\alpha(y)+2\theta^1\theta^2F(y),\qquad y=x+i\theta\sigma\bar\theta.$$

Thus the earlier mathematical components satisfy $\psi_{\mathrm{raw},\alpha}=\sqrt2\psi_\alpha$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$, while $\phi$ is unchanged. A component variation means coefficient extraction followed by this fixed conversion; it is not a rescaling of an integrated quantum field. Dimensions remain $[\phi]=1$, $[\psi]=3/2$, $[F]=2$.

The anti-automorphism gives $(\theta^1\theta^2F_{\mathrm{raw}})^*=-\bar\theta^{\dot1}\bar\theta^{\dot2}\bar F_{\mathrm{raw}}$. Consequently $I_D(\Phi^*\Phi)=-|F_{\mathrm{raw}}|^2$ in the pure auxiliary case, so the physical bracket gives $|F|^2$. The scalar term of the raw D integral is $4\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\bar\phi\partial_\nu\phi$ after compact-support integration by parts; the physical bracket gives $-\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\bar\phi\partial_\nu\phi$. These identities specify why the raw and physical component notations cannot be identified. Physical component potentials and coupling coefficients use the physical names above.

At fixed chiral coordinates define $P_{\mathrm{raw}}=\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot2}}\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot1}}|_{\bar\theta=0}=\bar D_{\dot2}\bar D_{\dot1}$. With $\epsilon_{12}=1$ and inverse $\epsilon^{12}=-1$, one has $\bar D^{\dot\alpha}\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-2P_{\mathrm{raw}}$ and $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\bar D^{\dot\alpha}=2P_{\mathrm{raw}}$. Under compact support or the stated vanishing-boundary condition the physical D-to-F transfer is

$$[U]_D=[P_{\mathrm{phys}}U]_F,\qquad P_{\mathrm{phys}}=-\frac12P_{\mathrm{raw}}=\frac14\bar D^{\dot\alpha}\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\frac14\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\bar D^{\dot\alpha}.$$

The order of contracted barred derivatives is therefore always part of a one-quarter projection formula. The identities follow directly by coefficient extraction and nilpotent coordinate translation, whose extra spacetime terms are total derivatives. They assert no boundary cancellation without that hypothesis.

items.title: Kähler coordinate-patch data for a rigid N=1 chiral model
items.design_state: Step 1 local definition added to supply an explicit prerequisite; see batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Give $\mathbb C^n$ the Euclidean topology transported from $\mathbb R^{2n}$ by the real coordinates $z^i=x^i+i y^i$, where $x^i,y^i\in\mathbb R$. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be open in this topology and contain $0$. Each complex number has its unique real decomposition $a+ib$ with $a,b\in\mathbb R$; write $\overline{a+ib}=a-ib$. A function on $U$ is smooth if all of its partial derivatives of every finite order in the real coordinates $(x^1,y^1,\ldots,x^n,y^n)$ exist and are continuous. Define the Wirtinger derivatives by $\partial_i=\tfrac12(\partial_{x^i}-i\partial_{y^i})$ and $\partial_{\bar i}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x^i}+i\partial_{y^i})$.

A **Kähler coordinate-patch datum** is such a pair $(U,K)$ with a smooth real-valued function $K:U\to\mathbb R$ for which the matrix $g_{i\bar j}(z,\bar z):=\partial_i\partial_{\bar j}K(z,\bar z)$ satisfies $g_{i\bar j}=\overline{g_{j\bar i}}$ and is positive definite: for every $z\in U$ and every nonzero $v=(v^1,\ldots,v^n)\in\mathbb C^n$, $\bar v^{\bar j}g_{i\bar j}(z,\bar z)v^i>0$. This smooth Hermitian matrix is the Kähler metric specified by the potential $K$. In natural units $\hbar=c=1$, mass dimensions are powers of mass; assign $[z^i]=1$, $[K]=2$, and $[g_{i\bar j}]=0$.

references.locator: §7.1, printed pp. 43–46: Kähler potentials, the Hermitian metric, and the chiral sigma-model action.

items.title: Rigid four-dimensional N=1 Wess–Zumino sigma-model action
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the exact planned contract; current inputs and open page-level readiness edges are recorded in batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use oriented and time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$. Let $n\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be an open set containing $0$, let $K:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, and require the Hermitian matrix $g_{i\bar j}(z,\bar z)=\partial_i\partial_{\bar j}K(z,\bar z)$ to be positive definite at every point of $U$. Let $W:U\to\mathbb C$ be smooth and holomorphic, where holomorphic means $\partial_{\bar i}W=0$ for every $i$, using the Wirtinger derivatives of the Kähler coordinate-patch definition; write $W_i=\partial_iW$. These data specify the Kähler coordinate patch and holomorphic superpotential of the model.

For these classical fields, take a finite-dimensional exterior algebra $\mathcal G$ over $\mathbb C$ on ordered odd generators $\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_m$ for $m\geq0$, with componentwise complex addition and multiplication modulo $\zeta_a^2=0$ and $\zeta_a\zeta_b=-\zeta_b\zeta_a$. Give it the conjugate-linear operation $(c\zeta_{i_1}\cdots\zeta_{i_r})^*=\bar c\zeta_{i_r}\cdots\zeta_{i_1}$, so $\zeta_a^*=\zeta_a$, $(uv)^*=v^*u^*$ and $(u^*)^*=u$. Reversing twice proves involutivity, and reversing the defining relations preserves them; thus this is a well-defined parity-preserving anti-automorphism. Write $\mathcal G_{\bar0},\mathcal G_{\bar1}$ for its even and odd subspaces, and use its degree-zero projection $b:\mathcal G\to\mathbb C$. Form the graded tensor product $\mathcal B=\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathbb C}\Lambda_4$ with the superspace Grassmann algebra, and let $\mathfrak J$ be the ideal of elements with zero total degree-zero part. Then $\mathfrak J^{m+5}=0$. For an even superfield $\Phi^i$, its body is its image under the augmentation $\mathcal B\to\mathbb C$ that applies $b$ and sends all superspace generators to zero; denote that ordinary scalar component by $\phi^i(x)$. Write $\bar\Phi^{\bar i}=(\Phi^i)^*$, $\nu^i=\Phi^i-\phi^i$, and $\bar\nu^{\bar i}=\bar\Phi^{\bar i}-\bar\phi^{\bar i}$; these differences lie in $\mathfrak J$. Define the smooth function's value on the full superfields by the finite nilpotent Taylor convention

$$K(\bar\Phi,\Phi):=\sum_{\substack{\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^n\\|\alpha|+|\beta|\leq m+4}}\frac{(\partial_z^\alpha\partial_{\bar z}^\beta K)(\phi,\bar\phi)}{\alpha!\,\beta!}(\nu)^\alpha(\bar\nu)^\beta,$$

where $\alpha!=\prod_i\alpha_i!$, $\beta!=\prod_i\beta_i!$, $\nu^\alpha=\prod_i(\nu^i)^{\alpha_i}$, $(\bar\nu)^\beta=\prod_i(\bar\nu^{\bar i})^{\beta_i}$, $\partial_z^\alpha=\prod_i\partial_i^{\alpha_i}$, $\partial_{\bar z}^\beta=\prod_i\partial_{\bar i}^{\beta_i}$, and the coefficient derivatives are evaluated at $(\phi(x),\bar\phi(x))$. Define the holomorphic superfield evaluation and its derivatives by the finite Taylor rule at the scalar body,

$$W(\Phi)(x,\theta,\bar\theta):=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq m+4}\frac{(\partial_z^\alpha W)(\phi(x))}{\alpha!}(\nu)^\alpha,\qquad W_i(\Phi):=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq m+4}\frac{(\partial_z^\alpha\partial_iW)(\phi(x))}{\alpha!}(\nu)^\alpha.$$

All terms beyond these finite sums vanish because $\mathfrak J^{m+5}=0$; the rule for $K$ is the Taylor extension of a smooth real function in its $z,\bar z$ variables, and the rule for $W$ uses only its holomorphic Wirtinger derivatives.

For each $i=1,\ldots,n$, the full formal physical components are smooth maps $a^i,\mathcal F^i:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar0}$ and $\psi^i_\alpha:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar1}$, with compact support in spacetime $M$: equivalently each coefficient of each exterior-basis monomial is a compactly supported smooth complex function of $x$. Require the scalar body $\phi^i=b(a^i)$ to lie in $U$ jointly. The lowest chiral coefficient is $a^i$, not merely its body $\phi^i$; it may have even nilpotent terms. In the physical normalization definition instantiate its scalar and auxiliary component symbols by $a^i$ and $\mathcal F^i$, respectively:

$$\Phi^i(y,\theta)=a^i(y)+\sqrt2\theta^\alpha\psi^i_\alpha(y)+2\theta^1\theta^2\mathcal F^i(y),\qquad y=x+i\theta\sigma\bar\theta.$$

Barred component fields mean the specified coefficient involution, so $\bar a^{\bar i}=(a^i)^*$ and $\overline{\mathcal F}^{\bar i}=(\mathcal F^i)^*$; barred fermions are likewise the conjugates of the coefficient maps. On $\mathcal B$ use the supplier's graded-tensor involution, including $\theta^*=\bar\theta$ and reversal of all factors. The formal action has values in the even fixed real subspace of $\mathcal G$; no order or nonnegativity is assigned to nilpotent elements.

The supersymmetry parameters $\epsilon^\alpha,\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}$ are constant odd coefficients, in $\mathcal G$ or a finite exterior extension equipped with the same involution. The adopted variation is $\delta\Phi^i=(\epsilon^\alpha Q_\alpha+\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}\bar Q_{\dot\alpha})\Phi^i$ with the chiral-superfield supercharges. Formal parameter components may be treated independently for the algebraic identities; a conjugation-preserving variation in this left-parameter convention has $\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}=-(\epsilon^\alpha)^*$ and $\delta\bar\Phi=(\delta\Phi)^*$. Indeed $\delta\theta=\epsilon$ and $\delta\bar\theta=-\bar\epsilon$ then commute with the chosen involution. The full even coefficient spaces for $a$ and $\mathcal F$ are retained under these transformations; the ordinary bosonic slice below need not be invariant. The engineering dimensions are $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[\theta]=[\bar\theta]=-1/2$, $[a^i]=1$, $[\psi^i]=3/2$, $[\mathcal F^i]=2$, $[K]=2$, and $[W]=3$ in mass units.

Adopt the classical action

$$S_{\mathrm{WZ}}=\int_M d^4x\left([K(\bar\Phi,\Phi)]_D+[W(\Phi)]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right),$$

where only the chiral F action has a Hermitian-conjugate partner and the D bracket is real; both physical brackets are the fixed multiples of the earlier raw ordered measures. The **ordinary bosonic sector** is the restriction $\psi=0$, $a=\phi\in\mathbb C^n$ and $\mathcal F=F\in\mathbb C^n$ with all positive-degree coefficient-algebra components set to zero; $\phi:M\to U$ and $F:M\to\mathbb C^n$ remain smooth and compactly supported in $M$. Thus taking this sector commutes with the degree-zero augmentation, but it is a restriction for evaluating a bosonic action, not an assertion of off-shell supersymmetry closure on a purely complex field space. The component conversion below gives its complete bosonic Lagrangian, up to the displayed spacetime divergence,

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bos}}=-g_{i\bar j}(\phi,\bar\phi)\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi^i\partial_\nu\bar\phi^{\bar j}+g_{i\bar j}(\phi,\bar\phi)F^i\bar F^{\bar j}+F^iW_i(\phi)+\bar F^{\bar j}\overline{W_j(\phi)}+\tfrac14\Box K(\phi,\bar\phi),\qquad\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu.$$

Its bosonic zero-derivative auxiliary terms are therefore precisely

$$\mathcal L_F=g_{i\bar j}(\phi,\bar\phi)F^i\bar F^{\bar j}+F^iW_i(\phi)+\bar F^{\bar j}\overline{W_j(\phi)}.$$

Only this ordinary complex sector is used for the ordered real scalar-potential and minimization conclusions. An arbitrary even $\mathcal G$-valued auxiliary field remains valid in the full formal model, but is not a vector in an ordered positive-definite complex metric space.

The canonical Wess–Zumino model is the special case $U=\mathbb C^n$, $K(z,\bar z)=\sum_i\bar z^{\bar i}z^i$, and hence $g_{i\bar j}=\delta_{i\bar j}$. This is an adopted classical formulation and normalization, not a deduction that nature realizes the model.

items.title: Four-dimensional N=1 non-Abelian vector superfield in connection normalization
items.design_state: Step 1 local addition authored to supply the specified scope or its missing explicit prerequisite; see batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use the selected smooth right-principal $SU(2)$ bundle $P\to M$ and its connection $A$ from the non-Abelian Yang–Mills model, with $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, and positive dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$. For each matter representation, let $V_R$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hermitian space and $R:SU(2)\to U(V_R)$ a smooth unitary representation; write $\rho_{R*}$ for its Lie-algebra differential. In the fundamental representation set $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $t_a=iT_a=\sigma_a/2$, so $\operatorname{Tr}_2(t_at_b)=\tfrac12\delta_{ab}$. In representation $R$, set $t_{a,R}=i\rho_{R*}(T_a)$. In a local trivialization write $V=V^at_a$ and $V_R=V^at_{a,R}$, and set $A_\mu=-i g_{\mathrm{YM}}B_\mu$ when $B_\mu=B_\mu^at_a$ is its vector component. Thus the matter covariant derivative is $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+\rho_{R*}(A_\mu)=\partial_\mu-i g_{\mathrm{YM}}B_\mu^at_{a,R}$.

A **vector superfield prepotential** is a dimensionless smooth even real matrix-valued superfield $V$ in the finite Grassmann-valued superspace of the N=1 chiral-superfield convention. Under a global rigid supersymmetry variation it transforms as $\delta V=(\epsilon^\alpha Q_\alpha+\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}\bar Q_{\dot\alpha})V$, with the supercharges defined in the chiral-superfield convention. Its local gauge transformations are $\Phi_R\mapsto e^{i\Lambda_R}\Phi_R$ and $e^{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}V_R}\mapsto e^{i\Lambda_R^\dagger}e^{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}V_R}e^{-i\Lambda_R}$, where $\Phi_R$ is chiral, $V_R=V^at_{a,R}$, and $\Lambda_R=\Lambda^at_{a,R}$ is a dimensionless chiral gauge-parameter superfield in the represented complexified Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}=\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$. The associated represented matrix curvature is defined by

$$\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}\!\left(e^{-2g_{\mathrm{YM}}V_R}D_\alpha e^{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}V_R}\right),$$

where $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\theta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$ and $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\theta^\beta\sigma^\mu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu$. Admissible vector-superfield data require $\bar D_{\dot\gamma}\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}=0$ and the adjoint transition law $\mathscr C_{\alpha,j}=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}\mathscr C_{\alpha,i}$ on each overlap with principal transition function $g_{ij}$.

Distinguish this represented curvature from the abstract connection-normalized Lie-algebra-valued curvature $\mathcal W_\alpha$. With canonical adjoint component field strength $W^a_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}$, the matrix convention is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}=2g_{\mathrm{YM}}t_{a,R}W^a_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}$, whereas $\mathcal W_\alpha=g_{\mathrm{YM}}T_aW^a_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}$. Since $t_{a,R}=i\rho_{R*}(T_a)$, their precise dictionary is

$$\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\frac{\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}}{2i}.$$

In the fundamental representation this gives $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)$, where $\kappa_{\mathbb C}=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2$ is evaluated on the Lie-algebra matrices $\mathcal W$, not on the raw $\mathscr C$. Thus the chiral action coefficient $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)/(4g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)$ equals $\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/(8g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)$, before adding its Hermitian conjugate. This is a fixed real-coupling classical normalization identity; it is not a quantum-field rescaling or measure identity. Both curvatures are chiral and have the corresponding conjugation/transition law. The abstract $\mathcal W$ has the connection-normalized gaugino and auxiliary components specified below.

In a local Wess–Zumino-gauge representative, the canonical component fields in the prepotential are a Hermitian gauge potential $B_\mu$, an adjoint Grassmann-odd Weyl gaugino $\lambda_{B,\alpha}$, and a real adjoint auxiliary field $D_B$, with expansion $V_{\mathrm{WZ}}=\theta\sigma^\mu\bar\theta B_\mu+i\theta^2\bar\theta\bar\lambda_B-i\bar\theta^2\theta\lambda_B+\tfrac12\theta^2\bar\theta^2D_B$. Here $\theta^2=\theta^\alpha\theta_\alpha$ and $\bar\theta^2=\bar\theta_{\dot\alpha}\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$ use the fixed antisymmetric spinor tensors. Their dimensions are $[B_\mu]=1$, $[\lambda_B]=3/2$, and $[D_B]=2$. The connection-normalized fields are $A_\mu=-ig_{\mathrm{YM}}B_\mu$, $\lambda=g_{\mathrm{YM}}\lambda_B$, and $D=g_{\mathrm{YM}}D_B$; hence $[A_\mu]=1$, $[\lambda]=3/2$, and $[D]=2$. The full prepotential is used for supersymmetry transformations; Wess–Zumino gauge is only a component representative and need not be preserved by an uncompensated supersymmetry variation.

items.statement: Use the rigid N=1 Wess–Zumino sigma-model postulate on $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, Kähler coordinate patch $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, smooth positive metric $g_{i\bar j}=\partial_i\partial_{\bar j}K$, holomorphic superpotential $W$, and full formal components $a^i,\mathcal F^i:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar0}$ and $\psi^i_\alpha:M\to\mathcal G_{\bar1}$ with coefficientwise compact support on $M$, using the involution and parameter conventions of the postulate. items.title: Kähler-metric F-term scalar potential in the rigid N=1 model
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the exact planned contract; current inputs and open page-level readiness edges are recorded in batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Use the rigid N=1 Kähler sigma-model action with scalar coordinates $z=(z^1,\ldots,z^n)\in U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, smooth real Kähler potential $K$, positive-definite Hermitian metric $g_{i\bar j}=\partial_i\partial_{\bar j}K$, holomorphic superpotential $W$, and complex algebraic auxiliary fields $F^i$. Use the ordinary complex bosonic sector of that postulate: all positive-degree coefficient-algebra components and fermions are set to zero, and the full formal even auxiliary coefficient is restricted to the complex field $F^i$. This restriction is for the potential calculation and does not assert supersymmetry closure on the restricted slice. With spacetime derivatives set to zero, write $W_i=\partial_iW(z)$ and $\bar W_{\bar j}=\partial_{\bar j}\overline{W(z)}$. The auxiliary Lagrangian is

$$\mathcal L_F=g_{i\bar j}F^i\bar F^{\bar j}+F^iW_i+\bar F^{\bar j}\bar W_{\bar j}.$$

Let $g^{i\bar j}$ be the inverse Hermitian matrix. The algebraic field equation is $F^i=-g^{i\bar j}\bar W_{\bar j}$, and eliminating $F$ gives the nonnegative scalar-potential contribution

$$V_F=g^{i\bar j}W_i\bar W_{\bar j}\geq0.$$

For the canonical Kähler potential $K=\sum_i\bar z^{\bar i}z^i$, this becomes $V_F=\sum_i|W_i|^2$. The simple sum is specific to that metric; for a noncanonical Kähler metric the inverse matrix in the displayed formula is required. This statement concerns the classical F-term sector only and does not include gauge D-terms or quantum corrections.

items.title: Rigid N=1 SU(2) gauge-matter superspace action
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the exact planned contract; current inputs and open page-level readiness edges are recorded in batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use the selected classical pure $SU(2)$ gauge model on oriented and time-oriented Minkowski $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, one selected smooth right-principal bundle $P\to M$, connection $A$, curvature $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, and positive dimensionless $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ from the non-Abelian Yang–Mills model. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[g_{\mathrm{YM}}]=0$, $[A_\mu]=1$, and $[F_{A,\mu\nu}]=2$. Let $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}$.

Choose a finite index set $I$ with $|I|\geq1$. For each $a\in I$, choose a finite-dimensional complex Hermitian space $V_a$, a smooth unitary representation $R_a:SU(2)\to U(V_a)$, and its associated vector bundle $E_a=P\times_{R_a}V_a$. Define $V_{\mathrm{mat}}=\bigoplus_{a\in I}V_a$ and $R_{\mathrm{mat}}(h)=\bigoplus_{a\in I}R_a(h)$. The matter field $\Phi^a$ is a smooth chiral superfield with local components in $E_a$ and unique full even scalar, odd left Weyl, and even auxiliary components $(a^a,\psi^a,\mathcal F^a)$ in the coefficient convention below; their engineering dimensions are $1$, $3/2$, and $2$. Let $V$ be the full real vector prepotential of the local vector-superfield definition, with connection-normalized component $A_\mu=-ig B_\mu$ in a local unitary frame, and let $\mathcal W_\alpha$ be its abstract connection-normalized Lie-algebra-valued chiral field strength. Its represented matrix curvature is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{-2gV_R}D_\alpha e^{2gV_R})$; the dictionary is $\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}/(2i)$, so in the defining representation $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)=\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/2$. The matter covariant derivative is $D_\mu\phi^a=\partial_\mu\phi^a+\rho_{a*}(A_\mu)\phi^a=\partial_\mu\phi^a-ig B_\mu^b t_{b,a}\phi^a$, where $t_{b,a}=i\rho_{a*}(T_b)$ and $T_b=-i\sigma_b/2$. Take smooth field-dependent component fluctuations with compact support in the local trivializing regions used for the action; noncompact backgrounds are treated only through compactly supported relative action differences.

Choose a holomorphic superpotential $W_G:V_{\mathrm{mat}}\to\mathbb C$ of engineering dimension three, where holomorphic means that every Wirtinger derivative $\partial_{\bar z^A}W_G$ vanishes in complex-linear coordinates $z^A$ on $V_{\mathrm{mat}}$. Require invariance under the induced $SU(2)$ action, $W_G(R_{\mathrm{mat}}(h)v)=W_G(v)$ for all $h\in SU(2)$ and $v\in V_{\mathrm{mat}}$. Its complex differential $dW_{G,v}:V_{\mathrm{mat}}\to\mathbb C$ is the complex-linear map with coordinate expression $dW_{G,v}(w)=\sum_A(\partial_{z^A}W_G)(v)w^A$. Write $\rho_{\mathrm{mat}*}(X)=\bigoplus_{a\in I}\rho_{a*}(X)$ for the infinitesimal representation. Differentiating the invariance condition along $h=\exp(tX)$ gives $dW_{G,v}(\rho_{\mathrm{mat}*}(X)v)=\sum_{a\in I}dW_{G,v}(0,\ldots,\rho_{a*}(X)v^a,\ldots,0)=0$ for every $X\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$.

In each local unitary frame, use the finite Grassmann convention of the Wess–Zumino model postulate for this complete finite matter family: take the finite exterior coefficient algebra $\mathcal G$ on $m$ odd generators with generator-fixing conjugate-linear, parity-preserving involutive anti-automorphism $(c\zeta_{i_1}\cdots\zeta_{i_r})^*=\bar c\zeta_{i_r}\cdots\zeta_{i_1}$ and its degree-zero augmentation, exactly as defined there, and let $\mathfrak J$ be the zero-body ideal in $\mathcal G\otimes\Lambda_4$, so $\mathfrak J^{m+5}=0$. Local full scalar and auxiliary components are smooth maps $a^a,\mathcal F^a$ into $\mathcal G_{\bar0}\otimes V_a$, and fermions into $\mathcal G_{\bar1}\otimes V_a$, with coefficientwise compact support on $M$ in the stated frames. Complex conjugation combines the specified $\mathcal G$ involution with the Hermitian dual in the unitary frame. The ordinary bosonic restriction sets all positive coefficient-algebra degrees and fermions to zero, giving complex fields $\phi^a=b(a^a)$ and $F^a=b(\mathcal F^a)$; it is not the formal field space used for off-shell closure. Use the full $\mathcal G$-valued action and coefficientwise supersymmetry variation, and the conjugation-compatible parameter convention of the Wess–Zumino postulate. Let $v(x)=(\phi^a(x))_{a\in I}$ be the body and $\nu(x,\theta,\bar\theta)=\Phi(x,\theta,\bar\theta)-v(x)\in\mathfrak J\otimes_{\mathbb C}V_{\mathrm{mat}}$ its nilpotent increment. Evaluate $W_G$ by the finite Taylor rule of the Wess–Zumino model postulate: after choosing complex-linear coordinates on $V_{\mathrm{mat}}$, write $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}V_{\mathrm{mat}}$ and let $\gamma=(\gamma_A)_{A=1}^d\in\mathbb N^d$ be a multi-index, with $\gamma!=\prod_A\gamma_A!$, $\partial_z^\gamma=\prod_A\partial_{z^A}^{\gamma_A}$, and $\nu^\gamma=\prod_A(\nu^A)^{\gamma_A}$.

$$W_G(\Phi)(x,\theta,\bar\theta):=\sum_{|\gamma|\leq m+4}\frac{(\partial_z^\gamma W_G)(v(x))}{\gamma!}\nu(x,\theta,\bar\theta)^\gamma,$$

where the finite Grassmann algebra and its nilpotent ideal are chosen for this finite component family as in that postulate. Thus the local expression is chiral and, by the stated $SU(2)$ invariance, defines the same scalar superpotential on overlapping associated-bundle frames. For a superspace superfield $X$, use the normalized physical brackets $[X]_D=-I_D(X)/4$ and, for chiral $Y$, $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$. Let $\kappa_\mathbb C$ denote the complex-bilinear extension of $\kappa$. Adopt the action

$$S_{\mathrm{GM}}=\int_M d^4x\left\{\sum_{a\in I}[\bar\Phi^a e^{2gV_{R_a}}\Phi^a]_D+\left(\left[\frac{1}{4g^2}\kappa_\mathbb C(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)+W_G(\Phi)\right]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\},$$

where $V_{R_a}$ is the represented vector prepotential from the local definition. Its coupling convention is fixed by requiring the bosonic gauge-curvature component to be exactly $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g^2)$; the same $g$ occurs in $e^{2gV_{R_a}}$ and in $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+\rho_{a*}(A_\mu)$, with no second gauge-coupling rescaling. The matter fields have $[\Phi^a]=1$, $[\psi^a]=3/2$, and $[F^a]=2$; $W_G$ has engineering dimension three. The model is defined locally in bundle trivializations with the transition laws induced by $P$; the D/F densities are required to obey the displayed supergauge law, with $\kappa$ invariant and $W_G$ gauge invariant, so the local action densities patch. Take configurations for which the action is integrable, or use compactly supported relative action differences with the same boundary convention as the supplied pure-gauge model. This is an adopted classical action, not a derivation that nature realizes it or that a quantum continuum theory exists. The gauge auxiliary field contributes its separate $D$-term sector; the $F$-term theorem on this page concerns only the chiral auxiliary contribution.

items.title: Off-shell supersymmetry of the rigid N=1 gauge-matter superspace action
items.design_state: Step 1 local addition authored to supply the specified scope or its missing explicit prerequisite; see batch-30 notes.
items.statement: For the adopted rigid N=1 SU(2) gauge-matter superspace action, use the full real vector prepotential $V$ and the chiral matter superfields $\Phi^a$ without fixing Wess–Zumino gauge. Use the full formal coefficient fields and the explicit order-reversing involution inherited from the gauge-matter postulate, with even scalar/auxiliary and odd fermion coefficients. Assume coefficientwise smooth compactly supported vector and matter component fluctuations on spacetime in the local trivializing regions used for the variation. The complex bosonic slice used for a scalar-potential calculation is not imposed during this off-shell variation. Under the global supertranslation $\delta=(\epsilon^\alpha Q_\alpha+\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}\bar Q_{\dot\alpha})$ with constant Grassmann-odd parameters, the variation of every full-superspace D-term is a sum of odd-coordinate derivatives and a spacetime divergence. The same is true of the chiral F-terms built from the gauge-invariant holomorphic superpotential and the chiral vector field strength. Compact support removes the spacetime boundary contributions, so the complete action is invariant. This is a conditional classical invariance statement for the full superspace fields; it does not assert that Wess–Zumino gauge is preserved by an uncompensated supersymmetry transformation.

items.title: Cubic one-field Wess–Zumino F-term potential
items.design_state: Step 1 local addition authored to supply the specified scope or its missing explicit prerequisite; see batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Take one chiral field with canonical Kähler potential $K(\bar\phi,\phi)=\bar\phi\phi$ and holomorphic superpotential $W(\phi)=\tfrac12m\phi^2+\tfrac16y\phi^3$, where $m\in\mathbb C$ has mass dimension one and $y\in\mathbb C$ is dimensionless. In the ordinary complex bosonic sector of the model postulate, take the auxiliary field to be complex-valued; the formal even coefficient space is retained before this restriction. For a smooth compactly supported scalar component $\phi:M\to\mathbb C$, the auxiliary equation and F-term potential are

$$F=-\overline{m\phi+\tfrac12y\phi^2},\qquad V_F=\left|m\phi+\tfrac12y\phi^2\right|^2.$$

This is a classical model calculation, not an empirical claim or a quantum effective potential.

items.title: Fundamental SU(2) chiral matter and its covariant derivative
items.design_state: Step 1 local addition authored to supply the specified scope or its missing explicit prerequisite; see batch-30 notes.
items.statement:
Choose the fundamental representation $R_{\mathrm f}:SU(2)\to U(\mathbb C^2)$ defined by $R_{\mathrm f}(h)w=hw$ for $h\in SU(2)\subset M_2(\mathbb C)$ and $w\in\mathbb C^2$, with the standard Hermitian form $w^\dagger z$ on $\mathbb C^2$. Its differential is $\rho_{\mathrm f*}(X)=X$ for $X\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and its Hermitian generators are $t_a=\sigma_a/2$. In a local trivialization write a scalar matter component as $\phi=(u,v)^T$ and the Hermitian vector potential as $B_\mu=B_\mu^at_a$, so the supplied connection is $A_\mu=-ig_{\mathrm{YM}}B_\mu$. The fundamental covariant derivative $D_\mu\phi=\partial_\mu\phi+\rho_{\mathrm f*}(A_\mu)\phi$ has components

$$D_\mu u=\partial_\mu u-\frac{i g_{\mathrm{YM}}}{2}\left(B_\mu^3u+(B_\mu^1-iB_\mu^2)v\right),\qquad D_\mu v=\partial_\mu v-\frac{i g_{\mathrm{YM}}}{2}\left((B_\mu^1+iB_\mu^2)u-B_\mu^3v\right).$$

On an overlap with transition $h(x)\in SU(2)$, the associated-bundle component is $\phi'=h^{-1}\phi$ and the right-connection local form is $A_\mu'=h^{-1}A_\mu h+h^{-1}\partial_\mu h$. Consequently $D_\mu'\phi'=h^{-1}D_\mu\phi$, so the scalar kinetic density $-(D_\mu\phi)^\dagger D^\mu\phi$ agrees in both local frames.
